message.content: Logistic regression is a statistical method used for predicting a binary outcome (e.g., yes/no, success/failure) based on one or more predictor variables. It models the probability that a given input belongs to a particular class using the logistic (sigmoid) function, which maps any real-valued number into the interval (0, 1). The model estimates coefficients for each predictor that maximize the likelihood of observing the given outcomes in the training data. Once fitted, logistic regression can be used to classify new observations by comparing the predicted probability to a chosen threshold (commonly 0.5).
